Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right mid-to-lower lung, with the later image (Figure 4), there is clear progression with increased density in the right lung and the appearance of new opacities in the left lung. This pattern of multifocal, progressive consolidation that mimics pneumonia but persists or spreads is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma).
